pr_title: Add new Use middleware extension method
pr_body:
## Description

Add a new `app.Use` overload that requires users to pass the `HttpContext` to the `next` function which will save 2 per-request allocations over the previous extension method.

## Customer Impact

Less per-request allocations when using simple middleware.

## Regression?
- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Risk
- [ ] High
- [ ] Medium
- [x] Low

[Justify the selection above]
Terminal middleware that used `app.Use` will need to update to use `app.Run` otherwise they'll get an ambiguous method compile error. We'd like to get this in early to get feedback on how bad that is, or if it isn't a problem.

## Verification
- [x] Manual (required)
- [x] Automated

## Packaging changes reviewed?
- [ ] Yes
- [ ] No
- [x] N/A

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/31463

-----

Main change is located at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/compare/brecon/use?expand=1#diff-e80bc3e234b6da05aea986e2aaa5b92bf492f085e00e7497d268e107169c9c6c
and
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/compare/brecon/use?expand=1#diff-dcc7a146ff62319dc1f9ab1847a9697596a4d899e7f75b588ed3c74d594ea305

The rest is changing all our tests and samples to use the new overload, or switch to `app.Run` if they never called `next`.

Should we file a breaking change announcement that people calling `app.Use` without calling `next` will be broken?

Note: We should apply this same change to the `ConnectionBuilder`
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/686da2e6c5b62570a7750bc3d85179ee5e9e75fd/src/Servers/Connections.Abstractions/src/ConnectionBuilderExtensions.cs#L42

TODO: File docs issue to update code to use new overload
pr_comments: I'm curious to get this into a preview and see if we get any feedback about it. People will only notice it on re-compile, and I wonder how obvious it will be if they need to switch to Run.
This should be in for preview4 if we're going to do it.

Hello human! Please make sure you've included the [Shiproom Template](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/docs/Servicing.md#submitting-a-fix-to-shiproom) in a comment or (preferably) the PR description. Also, make sure this PR is not marked as a draft and is ready-to-merge.
I see risk as more of "possibility of breaking your applications behavior unexpectedly". This wont break your apps behavior, you might just need to modify your code slightly to compile.

So compile-time breaking changes that don't change runtime behavior of apps that still compile without changes are considered "low" risk? And the number existing apps that work in .NET 5 and won't compile after this change has absolutely no impact on the risk?

I guess I can get behind that for previews since we can always revert and there's a simple code fix. I'm just surprised that's the standard.

I mean, that's my opinion, not a standard. And risk in this case doesn't mean the same thing as it does for patches and RC releases. If we were making a compile time breaking change in a patch, then this would be Extremely high risk.

But like you noted, since this is a preview and we can revert it later, low risk.

> Should we file a breaking change announcement that people calling app.Use without calling next will be broken?

Yes. What does the compile error look like exactly BTW?

>CS0121	The call is ambiguous between the following methods or properties: 'UseExtensions.Use(IApplicationBuilder, Func<HttpContext, Func<Task>, Task>)' and 'UseExtensions.Use(IApplicationBuilder, Func<HttpContext, RequestDelegate, Task>)'

issue_context.title: Non-allocating Use middleware extension method
comments: Looks like the compiler can disambiguate based on return value. I.e. when you type `await next()` vs. `await next(context)` it can figure out which one to use.
Which return value does intellisence recommend first?
The first one, and unfortunately it doesn't show multiple options when typing `next`. It does show the new one before the old one when typing `app.Use`.
That can be fixed. Lets not gate APIs on intellisense features that we can influence 😄
Do we want an analyzer to recommend the right overload? We don't want to obsolete the old one, that's used everywhere.
Is there a `[Recommend("use other")]` sort of thing that will just give a message and green squiggly in VS?

Thanks for contacting us.
We're moving this issue to the `Next sprint planning` milestone for future evaluation / consideration. Because it's not immediately obvious that this is a bug in our framework, we would like to keep this around to collect more feedback, which can later help us determine the impact of it. We will re-evaluate this issue, during our next planning meeting(s). 
If we later determine, that the issue has no community involvement, or it's very rare and low-impact issue, we will close it - so that the team can focus on more important and high impact issues.
To learn more about what to expect next and how this issue will be handled you can read more about our triage process [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/docs/TriageProcess.md).

We would like an analyzer to suggest the new method, but might just make an issue and backlog it as it isn't super high priority.

Add a `<para>` to the old methods doc comments to suggest using the new method.

File a docs issue to use the new overload in 6.0.
This seems like a poor use of `app.Use`. We should be recommending `app.Run` in this case. If we super cared about it, we can create an analyzer for this.

review_comments: Could you also add a quip about preferring `Run` if `next` is  unused?
